Call of Duty Black Ops 3 Begins 2016 at Top of UK Charts

I actually recently started playing the original Black Ops again and have been having quite a bit of fun with one of my old friends.

The biggest turn off I have for this game series now is just all the shitty tactics they use to make extra cash off the games. All the DLC and surplus transactions...

Not sure if that's still the case, I know CoD has dropped off somewhat in popularity recently. I'd honestly consider getting this game if they've improved on that a bit.

I think it really depends on what draws you to the series (campaign, multiplayer, or zombies), but I think Black Ops 3 is a pretty good deal. It has co-op campaign this time around, so you can play through the story mode with up to three other buddies. There's also a custom class system for campaign, so you can customize your operative. Beating campaign unlocks "nightmare mode", which replaces the baddies in campaign with zombies, and you play the missions in a revised order.

Zombies mode is pretty much par for the course for Black Ops, and isn't really what draws me to the series.

Multiplayer does a good job of incorporating a few minor changes without messing up the flow of combat. Jet packs have been revised so that they're no longer used for dodging as much as mobility. Level design incorporates multiple elevations now, so you can move around the level to great effect. Specialists let you customize your character a bit further, giving access to specialist-unique abilities that recharge every few minutes.

I ended up writing a summary of the game and its changes over at /v/GameReviews; you should check it out if you're interested in a bit more detail on what's new to the series. I didn't really care for Advanced Warfare, but I feel like they did a good job with Black Ops 3 even if they never come out with any DLC.

Very interesting. I may actually invest in this at some point then; the co-op campaign and the "nightmare mode" sound really interesting. From the few multiplayer combat vids I've seen the multiplayer gameplay seems to be at least relatively fun as well.

Now if only I had $50 to drop lol.

Yeah, I've been sidetracked by a few other games, but I'm happy with this one in a way I wasn't with Advanced Warfare. AW seemed rushed and a lot of the game mechanics (like jetpacks) weren't thought through. That was also Sledgehammer's first CoD, so it makes some sense. Black Ops 3 feels like it spent more time in the oven and came out well-made and with more content. It may not be worth spending $50 on if you didn't enjoy previous CoDs, but I'm sure waiting for a sale won't see any drop in the multiplayer population.

The biggest turn-off I had from CoD was the nightmare I first had with my old GTX-460 and the original Black Ops. Treyarch did a shit job of optimizing that game for the PC and it ran WAY worse on my card than was justifiable. I was getting better FPS with my old 8800GT at the time than with the 460.

The forums were infuriating. They kept locking any topics or other users who were using ATI cards or different families of nVidia cards would come in and just bandwaggon that it had to be a problem with the graphic driver or the OS. The game didn't run correctly for over a year at which point they finally resolved the bug and my FPS shot up by like 300%, but at that point the game was already almost obsolete as everyone was moving on to MW3 or whatever the next new one was.

That was like, 6 years ago though so I may be willing to give it another shot.

Ah, that's an important caveat; I've only played it on the Xbox One. In that case I'd recommend checking out some PC-specific reviews before you make up your mind. I haven't heard anything bad about it on the PC side, but it's worth double-checking.
